label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl, models/chumtoad.mdl: the judge does not know which
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: The silhouette in all ten views of sides.png is a plain rectangular box. The brief asks for a low, six-legged, wet crawler with a pale belly, and no legs, body taper or head show in any view, so the outline does not match the brief's words.

M2.reason: No size is given in the brief as a number, so there is no measured comparison (sizeAsked is null). The measured 12 x 10 x 6 is a flat, slab-like box, and in lineup.png it reads as larger than the roach and leech beside it, so it is clearly off a headcrab's proportions. Not scored 0 because the brief gives no number to test it against.

M3.reason: No parts are present. There are no six legs, no head, no ring of teeth and no pale belly in any view of sides.png or in the lineup. The model is one solid block.

M4.reason: The whole box is one flat neutral grey with a concrete-like mottle in every view. The brief asks for grey-green skin with a pale belly, and there is no green, no pale underside and no wet look. The belly, the one region the brief names separately, is no different from the back.

M5.reason: A faint mottled texture is present on every face, but the detail the brief asks for (the wet sheen, the teeth ring, the belly's markings) is absent. Nothing in the picture marks it as a creature.

M6.reason: In lineup.png, the grey box (C) sits beside the roach, leech and chumtoad at the same scale and is not any of them. A player would not take a plain box for a Half-Life creature, and the picture makes no case that it is a crawler. The path of these pictures names a decoy; the scoring stands on the pictures alone.

M7.reason: A box has no front: the front, back, left and right views are identical rectangles. There is no legs-down stance or head to orient, so the brief's facing cannot be seen. In run.png and attack.png it tumbles as a whole rather than standing on its origin like a crawler.

M8.reason: The measurements report 12 triangles and no SMAK check errors. The box is closed, with no open faces, inside-out faces or floating parts in any view, and the triangle count is far under the limit. This item is met, though the model fails every item that asks what the model is.

C1.reason: Across run.png (walk 0 to 34) and attack.png (jump 0 to 30), the whole box slides and tumbles as one rigid piece. No legs move, so nothing in the crawler's motion is shown. In several walk frames the box's base sits at or below the floor line, so it does not clearly stay on the floor.

C2.reason: The measurement reports that the model keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts (the contract line), so the game's own headcrab can play it. This is the one item the measurement supports fully.
